assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics unified electronic-structure and nuclear dynamics in one scheme, making finite-temperature ab initio simulation of condensed-phase chemistry, liquids, reactions and biomolecular active sites routine. It is a clear, original, foundational method with four decades of impact across chemistry, materials and biochemistry, close to the simulation-based tradition I know well.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper is a two-author work and the credit is unusually clean; a prize to Car and Parrinello fits within the three-laureate limit without leaving out a decisive contributor. Parrinello also appears elsewhere on the list (metadynamics, ML potentials), which could be argued either way but does not undermine this core attribution.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed by thousands of applications and many derived codes; the interpretation is stable and recognition is, if anything, overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to combine Parrinello's methods (metadynamics, ML potentials) into one broader citation.
I rely on memory for exact dates and priority and have not verified them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced protein degradation converts ubiquitin ligases into drug-programmable tools and has established a new therapeutic modality (PROTACs, molecular glues, degraders) with many compounds in clinical trials. It is a genuine game-changer in chemical biology and drug discovery, with a clear chemical idea (heterobifunctional molecules, rational design of ligase recruiters).
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated PROTACs; Ciulli supplied the structure-based design of VHL ligands and mechanistic work on ternary complexes. Handa/Ito (cereblon as thalidomide target) and Gray/Sakamoto/Kim are plausible alternative or additional recipients, so the three-person choice is contested.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent validation in cells and in clinical trials; first clinical efficacy data exist but approval of a PROTAC drug is still pending, so timing could be seen as slightly early.
uncertainties: Allocation among Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Handa and Gray is unresolved; the molecular-glue and PROTAC strands may need different recognition.
Clinical outcomes are not yet fully established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cytosine and adenine base editors enable programmable single-nucleotide chemical conversion in genomic DNA without double-strand breaks. This is an elegant chemistry-driven invention (engineered deaminases fused to Cas proteins) already moving into clinical use, and it extends the 2020 CRISPR prize in a distinct, chemical direction.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu led the invention and is clearly the decisive figure. Komor and Gaudelli were lead scientists in his laboratory and Nishida/Kondo made an independent early cytidine-deaminase editor, but a single-laureate or Liu-centered prize is the cleanest configuration.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely and in the clinic (early patient treatments); the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely but could reasonably wait for more clinical data.
uncertainties: Whether Nishida and Kondo's independent work should share credit.
Overlap with candidate B041 (prime editing) and with the 2020 prize could make the committee wary.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling provides general access to aryl amines and is used daily in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. It is an original, practical and widely adopted extension of the cross-coupling revolution recognized in 2010.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the ligand-controlled, general catalytic methods independently and decisively; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor with limited generality. A two-laureate prize is credible.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with broad industrial confirmation for roughly three decades. The main concern is that it is seen as continuing the 2010 prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2010 Nobel Prize in Chemistry and handling of Migita/Kosugi priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminator chemistry transformed biology and medicine and produced a many-orders-of-magnitude drop in sequencing cost. The chemistry of the nucleotide terminators and surface-bound clusters is central to the invention.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman originated the Solexa approach. Rothberg (454 pyrosequencing), Ju and Mayer contributed competing or complementary methods, so credit allocation among the first-generation NGS platforms is a real difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with unmatched impact, though sequencing itself has been recognized (Sanger 1980) and some may see it as more biology than chemistry.
uncertainties: Competing priority claims among platforms; chemistry versus biology classification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites achieved a very rapid rise in solar-cell efficiency, a striking materials-chemistry development with a potentially large energy impact. In the spirit of the committee's recent interest in new material classes, this is exciting and original, though the practical outcome is not yet settled.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cell, Park and Seok drove the solid-state efficiency breakthrough, and Snaith and Grätzel advanced the architecture; credit is dispersed among six names, with Kanatzidis also relevant. Any three-person selection is contested.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is confirmed independently, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercial viability remain open, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: The attribution dispute across at least six people is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs allow site-specific incorporation of noncanonical amino acids in living cells, and later work has reprogrammed codons and ribosomes. It gives chemists direct control over protein composition and has been broadly applied in biochemistry and drug development.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the method, Wang was the lead author on the first eukaryote/bacterial demonstrations in his group, and Chin extended it to multicellular organisms and to orthogonal ribosomes and quadruplet codons. Yokoyama and Mehl are also plausible; allocation is unclear.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated and widely adopted, although a transformative application is still developing.
uncertainties: Whether Schultz, Chin and Wang are the right three versus Yokoyama and Mehl.
Possible perception of overlap with directed evolution (2018).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative mass-spectrometry-based proteomics made proteome-scale identification and quantification of proteins routine and underlies much modern cell biology and clinical research. Its significance is high, though it builds on ionization methods awarded in 2002.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Yates and Aebersold are leading figures, but Hunt, Gygi and Heck also made decisive contributions (peptide sequencing, isotope tagging, shotgun methods), so the allocation is hard.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed, with continuing technical improvements; recognition is timely but diffuse.
uncertainties: Diffuse credit across several groups and possible classification as a technology-development prize rather than a single discovery.
